## Natural history notes

A tiny pygmy mole cricket characterized by its minute size, compact dark body, enlarged digging forelegs, and short hopping or jumping movements across sandy ground. In Florida, Ellipes gurneyi is found in patches of open sand, especially in dry scrub, sandhill, and similar sandy upland habitats, with records including the Panhandle and other parts of the state. It likely feeds on algae, detritus, and fine organic material at or just below the soil surface, while its small size makes it part of the sandy-ground food web for spiders, ants, predatory bugs, birds, and small reptiles.
